blocks.title: Palermo’s Cafe & Bakery
blocks.html: Located at 399 Liberty Street, Palermo's has been a Little Ferry institution since 1989, serving artisan brick-oven pizzas, paninis, sandwiches, and a full lineup of traditional Italian gourmet desserts that have earned it a devoted following well beyond the borough. The cafe also offers beer, wine, and cocktails alongside its food menu, and the custom cake shop has become one of the more sought-after destinations in the area for celebration cakes and specialty desserts. Indoor seating and a patio make it a natural gathering spot in any season.

blocks.title: Nikki’s Bar & Grill
blocks.html: Nikki's on Washington Avenue has established itself as one of Little Ferry's most lively spots since opening in 2017. The bar and grill features 14 TVs for sports viewing, eight draft beers, more than 25 bottled selections, and a menu of American and BBQ dishes headlined by the Tres Golpes burger and a rotating lineup of tacos and wings. Karaoke on Tuesdays and live DJs or bands on weekends keep the atmosphere consistently energetic, with a late-night kitchen running well past midnight most nights.

blocks.title: Losen Slote Creek Park
blocks.html: Losen Slote Creek Park occupies 28 acres of lowland forest and meadow right in Little Ferry, preserved since 1990 through a cooperative agreement with the New Jersey Meadowlands Commission. What makes the park distinctive is its layered natural history: the Losen Slote Creek itself was once a tidal tributary of the Hackensack River, later impounded to create the wetland habitat that now borders Mehrhof Pond, a former clay mining site that has gradually transformed into one of the area's most productive wildlife habitats. The trail through the park passes through a rich mix of damp woodland, shrub thicket, and open meadow, with botanical diversity and birdlife that reward visitors in every season.

blocks.title: Whiskey Roads Sports Bar
blocks.html: Whiskey Roads at 152 Washington Avenue describes itself as a premium dive experience, where the energy of a neighborhood tavern meets the atmosphere of a high-end whiskey lounge. The family-owned bar hosts live music, DJs, and comedy shows in partnership with the Meadowlands Comedy Club, along with a food menu that includes lunch specials, half-baby-back ribs, porterhouse steak, and a late-night kitchen that runs until 2:30 AM on weekends. The polished concrete floors and signature neon lighting give it a character that's distinctly its own.

blocks.title: Victoria's Mexican-American Grill
blocks.html: Victoria's at 201 Main Street is a mom-and-pop Mexican-American restaurant that has quietly built one of the strongest reputations on the local dining scene. The menu spans tacos, fajitas, chimichangas, coconut shrimp, housemade guacamole, and churros, with complimentary chips and black bean dip arriving at the table as a matter of course. Ranked among the top restaurants in the borough, it earns its following one honest, flavorful plate at a time. BYOB.

blocks.html: Lakeview Field, at 20 Indian Lake Road, sits along the shores of Indian Lake and is one of Little Ferry's most active outdoor recreational spaces. Baseball fields, open lawns, and access to waterside fishing make it a natural draw for residents year-round. The lakeside setting gives it a calm, unhurried character that feels removed from the borough's busier commercial corridors, yet is still close to everything.

items.q: What age do you need to be to receive a Lady L delivery in Little Ferry?

items.q: What's the purchase limit for a single delivery order?
items.a_html:
New Jersey caps each transaction at one ounce, or 28.35 grams, of usable cannabis. That ceiling covers all product types combined, broken down as follows:

  • Dried Flower/Bud: 28.35 grams (1 ounce).
  • Concentrates/Resin/Oils: 4 grams (solid or liquid/vaporized oil).
  • Ingestible Items (Gummies/Edibles): 1,000 mg of THC (roughly ten 100mg packages).
  • Maximum Possession Limit: Up to 6 ounces of cannabis and cannabis products.
  • Mixing Products: You can mix and match, for example, by purchasing 1/2 ounce of flower and 2 grams of concentrates.
  • Daily Limits: The 1-ounce limit is generally considered a daily limit across all dispensaries.

items.q: What taxes come with a Little Ferry cannabis delivery order?
items.a_html: New Jersey adult-use cannabis carries three charges: a 6.625% state sales tax, a $2.50-perounce Social Equity Excise Fee (SEEF), and a 2% municipal transfer or user tax in municipalities that have authorized it. All applicable charges appear at checkout before your order is finalized, so there are no surprises on the back end.
